candidate_tools.description: Creates a new file in Google Drive from provided text content (up to 10MB), supporting various formats including automatic conversion to Google Workspace types. Returns flat metadata fields (`id`, `mimeType`, `name`) at the top level — not nested under a `file` object. Created files are private by default; use a sharing tool afterward for collaborative access. Rapid successive calls may trigger `403 rateLimitExceeded` or `429 userRateLimitExceeded`; apply exponential backoff between retries. Does not support shared-drive targets in all cases.
Tool to update values in ranges matching data filters. Use when you need to update specific data in a Google Sheet based on criteria rather than fixed cell ranges.

Tool to create a permission for a file or shared drive. Use when you need to share a file or folder with users, groups, domains, or make it publicly accessible. **Warning:** Concurrent permissions operations on the same file are not supported; only the last update is applied.

DEPRECATED: Use GOOGLEDRIVE_COPY_FILE_ADVANCED instead. Duplicates an existing file (not folders) in Google Drive by `file_id`; copy lands in same folder as original — use GOOGLEDRIVE_MOVE_FILE afterward for precise placement. Copy receives a new `file_id`; update stored references accordingly. For shared drives, requires organizer/manager rights.

case.rationale: The task requires creating a new document from text input and then sharing that newly created file with a colleague. This naturally maps to the file creation tool followed by the permission-granting tool, representing a standard collaborative workflow.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Step]: Create the analysis report in one pass using GOOGLEDOCS_CREATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN (title + one consolidated markdown body with headings, findings, and references w/ clickable links).
[Optional (if markdown creation fails)] [Fallback]: Create a blank starter using GOOGLEDOCS_CREATE_DOCUMENT (capture document_id for all later edits).

[Optional (if content is too large/table-heavy or must be chunked)] [Next Step]: Insert/replace sections iteratively using GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_SECTION_MARKDOWN (keep structure, tone, and citations consistent).

[Optional (if structured comparisons are needed)] [Next Step]: Add tables using GOOGLEDOCS_INSERT_TABLE_ACTION (metrics/pros-cons matrix), then surround/fill text via GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_SECTION_MARKDOWN.
[Optional (if rewriting the whole doc is easier than section edits)] [Next Step]: Overwrite/refine the full document using GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN (final polish pass).
[Optional (if adding figures/infographics)] [Next Step]: Generate visuals using GEMINI_GENERATE_IMAGE (produce a usable image asset).
[Optional (if an image asset is available)] [Next Step]: Embed visuals using GOOGLEDOCS_INSERT_INLINE_IMAGE (add captions/placement tweaks via GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN if needed).
known_pitfalls: [GOOGLEDOCS_CREATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN] Requires an authorized Google Docs connection; auth failures prevent creation/editing.

[GOOGLEDOCS_CREATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN] Observed 400 Bad Request: "Multiple tables (8) detected. Only ONE table is allowed per call" on markdown_text; remove/simplify table-like markdown or split via GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_SECTION_MARKDOWN.
[GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN] Complex markdown (nested lists/tables) may not render as expected—plan a quick follow-up formatting pass.
[GOOGLEDOCS_INSERT_INLINE_IMAGE] Images must be reachable and in supported raster formats (PNG/JPEG/GIF); SVG often won’t embed.
[GEMINI_GENERATE_IMAGE] Produces image assets only; pass the usable asset/location into GOOGLEDOCS_INSERT_INLINE_IMAGE (don’t rely on markdown image links).

GOOGLEDOCS_CREATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN.description: Creates a new Google Docs document, optionally initializing it with a title and content provided as Markdown text.

title.description: The title for the new Google Docs document.

name.description: The filename that will be used when uploading the file to the destination service

s3key.description: The S3 key of a publicly accessible file, typically returned from a previous download action that stored the file in S3. This key references an existing file that can be uploaded to another service.

mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file

file.description: Uploaded image file. The action converts it into a temporary public URL that Google Docs can fetch.

name.description: Name used to reference the uploaded image from Markdown, for example attachment://diagram or ./diagram.png.

image_assets.description: Optional uploaded images that Markdown can reference by name. Use Markdown image syntax like ![Alt](attachment://diagram). Public HTTPS image URLs in markdown do not need image_assets.

markdown_text.description: The initial content for the document, formatted as Markdown. Also accepts 'content' as an alias. Supports headings, real Google Docs lists including nested lists, multiple Markdown tables, task-list markers, images via publicly accessible URLs or matching image_assets uploads (max 2KB URL length after resolution; formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF; SVG not supported), blockquotes, code blocks, hyperlinks (e.g., [text](url)), and text formatting (bold, italic, etc.). If empty or omitted, creates document with title only.

GOOGLEDOCS_CREATE_DOCUMENT.description: Creates a new Google Docs document using the provided title as filename and inserts the initial text at the beginning if non-empty, returning the document's ID and metadata (excluding body content).

examples: This document outlines the key findings...
text.description: Optional initial text content to insert at the beginning of the new document. If not provided, an empty document will be created. For very large text (over 50,000 characters), the text will be inserted in chunks to avoid API limits.

title.description: Title for the new document, used as its filename in Google Drive.

GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_SECTION_MARKD.description: Tool to insert or replace a section of a Google Docs document with Markdown content. Use when you need to update only a section of a document by specifying start and optional end indices. Supports full Markdown formatting.

tab_id.description: Optional tab ID to update with the rendered Markdown. When omitted, the first tab is updated.

end_index.description: Optional one-based end index of the content to replace (exclusive); must be greater than or equal to start_index. If end_index is not provided, the content is inserted at the start_index without replacing existing content. Requires start_index to be provided - if start_index is omitted (append mode), end_index is ignored. Important: Use the exact indices from GOOGLEDOCS_GET_DOCUMENT_BY_ID without modification. The Google Docs API does not allow deleting the last newline character of a document segment (body, header, footer, etc.), so ensure end_index does not include the final segment newline.

document_id.description: The unique ID of the Google Docs document to update. This is the alphanumeric string found in the document URL: https://docs.google.com/document/d/{DOCUMENT_ID}/edit. Valid IDs are typically 44 characters long and contain only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores (e.g., '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms'). To get a document ID: create a new document using GOOGLEDOCS_CREATE_DOCUMENT, or extract it from an existing document's URL. Also accepts parameter aliases: 'id', 'doc_id', 'documentId', or 'docId'.

start_index.description: One-based UTF-16 code unit index where to insert or start replacement. If not provided, content will be appended to the end of the document. Use 1 to insert at the very beginning of the document. To insert at a specific position, first use GOOGLEDOCS_GET_DOCUMENT_BY_ID to retrieve the document structure and find the desired index from the body.content elements' start_index/end_index values. If the provided index equals or exceeds the document segment's end index, it will be automatically adjusted to the last valid position (end_index - 1) and a message will be included in the response.

markdown_text.description: Markdown content to insert or replace in the document section. Large content is automatically split into smaller batches to avoid API limits. Also accepts 'markdown', 'content', 'text', 'body', 'markdownText', or 'markdown_content'.
